sources.title: Brain-to-brain coupling during handholding is associated with pain reduction
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
sources.why_it_matters: Recorded dual-EEG hyperscanning across 22 romantic couples during thermal pain, proving partner handholding synchronizes 8-12 Hz alpha-mu brain waves across both brains in direct proportion to pain relief.

sources.title: Lending a Hand
sources.why_it_matters: Scanned 16 married women facing ankle electric-shock threats on fMRI alone, holding a stranger's hand, or holding their husband's hand — showing spouse handholding broadly quieted threat circuits, especially in high-quality marriages.

sources.title: Do partner handholding effects linger? Order effects of handholding support on mechanical hypersensitivity in women
sources.why_it_matters: Tested mechanical pain modulation and carryover order effects of partner handholding support.

sources.title: Dissociation between individual differences in self-reported pain intensity and underlying fMRI brain activation
sources.why_it_matters: Mapped individual variability between subjective pain reports and fMRI pain representations.

sources.title: A Picture's Worth
sources.why_it_matters: Demonstrated that holding a romantic partner's hand (and attachment safety cues) significantly reduces experimental thermal pain ratings compared with stranger or object control conditions.

sources.title: Does Rejection Hurt? An fMRI Study of Social Exclusion
sources.why_it_matters: Seminal Science fMRI study proving social separation/exclusion recruits dorsal anterior cingulate and anterior insula — the exact affective pain matrix calmed by partner touch.
